column5: Damek, may I speak with you?
column6: 达梅克，我能和你说句话吗？

column5: Oh, of course. \nIs everything okay...?
column6: 哦，当然。\n一切都还好吗……？

column5: I believe you've been waiting for this?
column6: 我想你一直在等这个吧？

column5: He hands Damek the piece of paper in his grip.{w}\nSoon after, he returns to scribbling in his ledger.
column6: 他把手里攥着的那张纸递给达梅克。{w}\n随即便继续在账本上写写画画。

column5: Secure a naval army...?\nThat's a lot bigger than our initial plans.
column6: 组建一支海军……？\n这可比我们最初的计划大得多。

column5: Is it an unwelcome change?
column6: 这变化不受欢迎吗？

column5: Spice stands waiting, ready to record Damek's response.
column6: 斯派斯站在一旁等待，准备记录下达梅克的回答。

column5: No, not at all.\nWe were just planning to steal The Triumvirate's ships.\nWhile they were busy with Valinorth, they'd be unmanned.
column6: 不，完全不会。\n我们原本只打算偷三人执政团的船。\n趁他们忙于瓦利诺斯的时候，那些船无人看守。

column5: But this...?\nIt could grow our forces exponentially.\nEspecially if the pirates lend us their army.
column6: 但这个……？\n它能让我们的兵力成倍增长。\n尤其是如果海盗愿意借兵给我们。

column5: Not for free, of course.\nThey'll probably rob Gryz blind in exchange.\nI recommend not offering them any of our resources.
column6: 当然不是白帮忙。\n作为交换，他们大概会把格瑞兹榨得一滴不剩。\n我建议不要拿我们的任何资源去换。

column5: We barely have enough food for our own men.\nAnd weapons for that matter. We need more of those.\nDo you think you could spin negotiations in our favor?
column6: 我们自己人连口粮都勉强够用。\n武器也一样，我们需要更多。\n你觉得你能把谈判引向对我们有利的方向吗？

column5: Of course I can.\nI'm nothing if not a good negotiator.\nIt seems like everything is in our favor.
column6: 那当然。\n别的不敢说，我绝对是个谈判高手。\n看起来一切都在朝对我们有利的方向发展。

column5: This final clause, however...
column6: 不过，最后这一条……

column5: The one requesting The Seer's presence?\nPay it no mind, they should be arriving here shortly.\nIn fact — I'll go meet them in the town square right away.
column6: 要求先知到场的那条？\n别在意，他们应该很快就会到。\n其实——我这就去城广场接他们。

column5: The one requesting The Seeress' presence?\nPay it no mind, they should be arriving here shortly.\nIn fact — I'll go meet them in the town square right away.
column6: 要求先知到场的那条？\n别在意，他们应该很快就会到。\n其实——我这就去城广场接他们。

column5: Is their Exodus training regiment finalized?\nYour schedule should be able to accommodate changes.\nYour plan is still slow exposure to develop a tolerance, yes?
column6: 他们的流亡训练计划定下来了吗？\n你的日程应该还能调整。\n你的方案还是逐步接触、培养耐受，对吧？

column5: Yeah, that's the best way to do it.\nI could only handle it for a mere moment.\nBut I feel stronger — like I could handle more.
column6: 是啊，这是最好的办法。\n我只能撑住短短一瞬。\n但我感觉自己变强了——好像能撑得更久。

column5: Of course, I'm not going to touch it again.\nI'm just assuming the same rules apply to The Seer.\nWith controlled exposure, they could wield it longer and longer.
column6: 当然，我不会再去碰它了。\n我只是假设同样的规则也适用于先知。\n通过有控制的接触，他们能使用得越来越久。

column5: Of course, I'm not going to touch it again.\nI'm just assuming the same rules apply to The Seeress.\nWith controlled exposure, they could wield it longer and longer.
column6: 当然，我不会再去碰它了。\n我只是假设同样的规则也适用于先知。\n通过有控制的接触，他们能使用得越来越久。

column5: Long enough to aid our final assault on Balteus.
column6: 久到足以协助我们对巴尔泰乌斯的最后一击。

column5: As we take our first steps away from Valinorth, I make note of my surroundings.{w}\nNot much has changed, yet in my heart, I can feel an indescribable difference.{w}\nCrimson leaves litter the ground, remnants of the earlier spectacle.
column6: 当我们迈出离开瓦利诺斯的第一步时，我留意着四周。{w}\n景物没有太大变化，可我心里却能感到一种难以言说的不同。{w}\n绯红的落叶铺满地面，是方才那场奇景的残迹。

column5: They look pretty cool, huh?
column6: 它们看起来挺酷的吧？

column5: It was definitely a nice send-off.\nI just hope the Mazeans aren't afraid.
column6: 这场送行确实不错。\n我只希望马泽奥人不会害怕。

column5: Why would they be afraid...?
column6: 他们为什么会害怕……？

column5: Really...? But they're just leaves.
column6: 真的吗……？可它们只是叶子啊。

column5: You know how superstitious people can be.
column6: 你知道人有多迷信。

column5: Well, the rest of Alestia sees them as an ill omen.
column6: 唉，阿莱斯蒂亚其他地方的人都把它们当成凶兆。

column5: But they're just leaves...
column6: 可它们只是叶子啊……

column5: Well, you know how superstitious people can be.
column6: 唉，你知道人有多迷信。

column5: I was taught that they're tears from the spirit realm.\nYou know, the spirits crying out. But I don't know {i}why{/i}.\nPerhaps our parents were reaching out to us...?
column6: 我听说它们是灵界流下的眼泪。\n就是灵在哭喊。可我不知道{i}为什么{/i}。\n也许是我们父母在试着联系我们……？

column5: Case in point, Pro.
column6: 这就是活生生的例子，普洛。

column5: Fair enough.\nAnyway, there was something I had to say.\nDon't you think it's a little odd to walk around like that...?
column6: 说得也是。\n总之，我有件事得说。\n你不觉得就那样到处走有点奇怪吗……？

column5: Excuse me!? That's not what I meant!\nI'm talking about that huge blade you have on your back!\nThe Triumvirate might have eyes in Mazeo. We need to cover it up.
column6: 什么！？我不是那个意思！\n我说的是你背上的那把巨刃！\n三人执政团在马泽奥可能有眼线。我们得把它遮起来。

column5: Actually, that's kind of what I had in mind.\nI don't think you should walk around with that Blade out in the open.\nLet's cover it up, alright? There might be spies in Mazeo.
column6: 其实，我正有此意。\n我觉得你不该把那把刃明晃晃地背在身上到处走。\n我们把它遮起来，好吗？马泽奥可能有间谍。

column5: What!? No! That's not what I meant at all.\nI'm talking about The Blade of Exodus, you know.\nWe need to cover it up so nobody sees it.
column6: 什么！？不！我完全不是那个意思。\n我说的是流亡之刃，你懂的。\n我们得把它遮起来，别让人看见。

column5: Yeesh, I'm just trying to help you out!\nIn Mazeo, there's eyes and ears everywhere. Spies, even.\nWe can't have you walk around with that blade so openly.
column6: 啧，我只是想帮你而已！\n在马泽奥，到处都是眼睛和耳朵，甚至还有间谍。\n我们不能让你就这么明晃晃地背着那把刃到处走。

column5: That huge blade you have on your back...?\nYou know, the one The Triumvirate will want to steal?\nI think we should cover it up. It's too open right now.
column6: 你背上的那把巨刃……？\n就是三人执政团想抢走的那把？\n我觉得我们该把它遮起来。现在太显眼了。

column5: That's actually a good idea.\nWe don't know how many eyes will be on us.\nIt might help us get past the gate guard, as well.
column6: 这主意其实不错。\n我们不知道会有多少双眼睛盯着我们。\n它也许还能帮我们过城门守卫那一关。

column5: Yeah, they wouldn't take kindly to seeing that.\nThey're skeptical enough of travellers from Valinorth.
column6: 是啊，他们看到那玩意儿可不会高兴。\n他们对瓦利诺斯来的旅人本来就够戒备的了。

column5: What!? But we wouldn't do anything!
column6: 什么！？可我们又不会做什么！

column5: That's exactly the point.
column6: 问题就出在这儿。

column5: People from Valinorth would never harm Mazeo, true.\nBut that's what makes it the perfect excuse for wrongdoers.\nSay you're from Valinorth, and get through without a second thought.
column6: 瓦利诺斯的人确实绝不会伤害马泽奥。\n但正因如此，它才成了坏人最完美的借口。\n说一句你来自瓦利诺斯，就能毫无阻碍地通过。

column5: That's awful!
column6: 太可恶了！

column5: Yeah. Unfortunately they're keen on that trick.\nThey'll end up questioning us no matter what we say.
column6: 是啊。可惜他们对这套把戏很在行。\n不管我们怎么说，最后都会被盘问。

column5: So we need to cover up the blade...
column6: 所以我们需要把刃遮起来……

column5: Yeah.
column6: 嗯。

column5: I guess it's a good thing I brought this, then.
column6: 那我带了这东西来，算是件好事。

column5: She holds up the cloth that was wrapping the blade in The Grand Tree.{w}\nIt's large enough that I could wrap it around myself like a cloak.{w}\nI'm positive that they'll ask what's underneath, but it's worth a try.
column6: 她举起在巨树里包裹那把刃的布。{w}\n它足够大，我可以像披风一样裹在身上。{w}\n我敢肯定他们会问布下面是什么，但值得一试。

column5: What do we do if they don't buy it?
column6: 要是他们不上当怎么办？

column5: Well, I'll play some of my patented charm.
column6: 那我就施展一下我那招牌魅力。

column5: We're doomed.
column6: 我们完蛋了。

column5: Fortaime and Valessa share a quick laugh, while Pro fumes.{w}\nUlric crosses his arms, and starts to come up with a plan.
column6: 福泰姆和瓦莱莎相视一笑，普洛则气得冒烟。{w}\n乌尔里克抱起双臂，开始琢磨对策。

column5: There's still a long way to go, so let's walk and talk.\nWe're losing time, and that's the one thing we can't afford to lose.
column6: 还有很长的路要走，我们边走边说吧。\n我们在浪费时间，而时间恰恰是我们最耗不起的。

column5: Immediately after, Valessa hands me the cloth from earlier.{w}\nI knew that many people in Mazeo were part of The Rebellion, but not everybody.{w}\nThe Gate Guards must be an example of those not under Damek's thumb. At least yet.
column6: 紧接着，瓦莱莎把刚才那块布递给我。{w}\n我知道马泽奥有很多人属于反抗军，但并非所有人。{w}\n城门守卫大概就是不受达梅克掌控的那一类人。至少目前还不是。

column5: Alright...
column6: 好吧……

column5: I wrap the cloak around my back, and fashion the top into a hood.{w}\nThe Blade of Exodus, as well as my identity, was sufficiently masked.{w}\nWith the small hope that this facade will work, we continue toward Mazeo.
column6: 我把布裹在背上，将上端做成兜帽。{w}\n流亡之刃和我的身份都被很好地遮掩住了。{w}\n怀着这伪装能奏效的一丝希望，我们继续朝马泽奥前进。

column5: So, about that charm...
column6: 那么，关于那个魅力……

column5: Yeah?
column6: 嗯？

column5: When are you gonna start turning it on?
column6: 你打算什么时候开始施展？

column5: It's... been on this whole time.
column6: 它……一直都开着呢。

column5: Oh boy...
column6: 老天啊……

column5: Hey, what's that supposed to mean?
column6: 喂，那是什么意思？

column5: It means you think highly of your own ability.\nAnd if I'm not mistaken, it's a little {i}too{/i} highly.
column6: 意思是你把自己的本事看得太高了。\n如果我没说错，是高得有点{i}过头{/i}了。

column5: That's not true!
column6: 才不是！

column5: Oh really? Charm me, then.
column6: 哦，是吗？那你来魅惑我试试。

column5: You mean right now...?
column6: 你是说现在……？

column5: Yeah, right here. Right now.\nShouldn't be too hard for someone like yourself.
column6: 对，就这儿，就现在。\n对你这样的人来说应该不难吧。

column5: Oh, well...\nJust let me think.\nIt takes a bit to \"get in the groove\".
column6: 哦，这个……\n让我想想。\n总得花点时间“进入状态”。

column5: Oh, is that so? Sounds like an excuse to me.
column6: 哦，是这样吗？在我看来像是借口。

column5: It's not!
column6: 才不是！

column5: Alright then, just hurry it up, Pro.\nI'd tell you to take your time, but I don't want to die of old age.
column6: 那好吧，快点，普洛。\n我本想让你慢慢来，可我不想等得老死。

column5: Hmph!
column6: 哼！

column5: Hey.
column6: 嘿。

column5: There's not much to say, that you don't already know.\nIt's a trading hub, providing goods and services to Valinorth and Alarinthia.\nBut there's a large piracy scene, providing the more... \"illicit\" goods and services.
column6: 该说的你大概都知道了。\n这里是个贸易枢纽，为瓦利诺斯和阿拉林西亚提供货物与服务。\n不过海盗活动也很猖獗，提供一些更……“见不得光”的货物与服务。

column5: The Occupation was supposed to make things better, but it didn't.\nIt only created more laws to break, and they haven't even cracked down on them.\nThe Mayor has slowly defected to our side, after realizing The Triumvirate's true intent.
column6: 占领本该让情况变好，结果却没有。\n它只是凭空多出一堆可以被违反的法律，而他们连这些法律都懒得执行。\n市长在看清三人执政团的真实意图后，已经慢慢倒向我们这边。

column5: They only wanted the Spirit Idol hidden underneath Mazeo. We're sure of it.\nThe introduction of law and order to the city of Mazeo was justification enough for them.\nIf they truly wanted to keep Mazeo in line, they'd be enforcing the laws they put in place.
column6: 他们想要的只是藏在马泽奥地下的灵像。我们很确定。\n对马泽奥城引入法律与秩序，对他们来说就是充足的借口。\n如果他们真想管住马泽奥，就该执行自己定下的法律。

column5: His name is Gryz, and he's slowly defected to our side.\nHe's a good ally to have, especially with the strings he can pull.\nI doubt our plans would've gotten this far without his assistance.
column6: 他叫格瑞兹，已经慢慢倒向我们这边。\n他是个很有用的盟友，尤其是他手里能牵动的那些关系。\n要是没有他的帮助，我们的计划恐怕走不到这一步。

column5: He took part in The Occupation actually, and slowly realized he was wrong.\nSo that would mean he's been in power for a little over twenty years.\nHe was pretty distant at first, but we slowly got more in touch with him.
column6: 其实他也参与过占领，后来慢慢意识到自己错了。\n也就是说，他掌权已经有二十多年了。\n起初他对我们很疏远，但我们慢慢和他建立了更多联系。

column5: As time passed, he realized he was being lied to. That's what The Triumvirate does.\nThey tell you that you're getting what you want — but it's just a cover to use you.\nI guess he got fed up, and realized that The Rebellion could actually deliver.
column6: 随着时间推移，他意识到自己一直被欺骗。三人执政团就是这么干的。\n他们让你以为你得偿所愿——但那不过是利用你的幌子。\n我猜他是受够了，也明白反抗军才真能兑现承诺。

column5: I'd say so, yeah. This isn't a sudden defection, or anything like that.\nIt's been slowly happening over the last twenty years. I saw it all.\nHe's truly sorry for what he's done, and now he wants redemption.
column6: 我想是的。这不是突然倒戈之类的戏码。\n过去二十年里，这一切是慢慢发生的。我全都看在眼里。\n他真心为自己做过的事感到抱歉，如今想要赎罪。

column5: I guess joining us will help him achieve that redemption.\nHe's just in the unfortunate situation of \"playing both sides\".\nHe does {i}work{/i} with the enemy, but his allegiance is with us. I know it.
column6: 我想加入我们能帮他实现那份赎罪。\n他只是不幸处在“两头周旋”的境地。\n他确实为敌人{i}做事{/i}，但他的忠诚属于我们。我清楚。

column5: They'd probably kill him. They don't really tolerate that.\nBut it's not very often that somebody goes against their rule.\nThey seem to have a \"sway\" over their subjects. It's hard to describe.
column6: 他们大概会杀了他。他们容不下这种事。\n不过敢违抗他们统治的人并不多见。\n他们似乎对治下的人有一种“支配力”。很难形容。

column5: Like — only now that he's away from them is his mind finally clear.\nAs soon as they find out, I'm sure they'll make him a primary target.\nI'm willing to bet that they'll send Sovy and his Apprentice to do the job.
column6: 就像——直到现在远离了他们，他的头脑才终于清醒。\n一旦他们发现，我敢肯定他们会把他列为首要目标。\n我敢打赌，他们会派索维和他的学徒来动手。

column5: He's really big. He can be intimidating, but his heart is in the right place.\nYou don't really get the \"politician\" vibe from him. He looks more like a warrior.\nBut that's kind of the point. The Triumvirate wanted a ruthless man in charge.
column6: 他身材魁梧，看着挺吓人，但心地很好。\n你从他身上感受不到什么“政客”气息，他更像一名战士。\n但这正是关键所在。三人执政团想要的就是个冷酷无情的人来掌权。

column5: Just don't judge him based on his appearance, and you'll be fine.\nThere's a friendly man underneath that hardened exterior. I promise.\nIf it weren't for his efforts, The Rebellion would barely be successful.
column6: 别以貌取人就好，这样就没问题。\n那副强硬的外表下是个友善的人，我保证。\n要不是他的努力，反抗军根本不可能成功。

column5: No, and why would it? It was just a front because they wanted the Spirit Idol.\nMazeo remains largely the same. Attention was just diverted to different areas.\nFor example, trade bans just made the pirates focus on different commodities.
column6: 没有，又怎么会呢？那只是个幌子，因为他们想要灵像。\n马泽奥大体上还是老样子，只是注意力被引到了别的领域。\n比如，贸易禁令只是让海盗转而盯上别的商品。

column5: They talked a big talk, but they didn't follow through. It was all a lie.\nFor example, The Rebellion formed effortlessly under their \"watchful eyes\".\nUnder competent rulers, that never should've happened. See what I'm getting at?
column6: 他们嘴上说得漂亮，却从不兑现。全是谎言。\n比如，反抗军就在他们“警觉的注视”下毫无阻碍地组建起来了。\n要是换成有能力的统治者，这种事根本不可能发生。明白我的意思吗？

column5: How else do you explain the huge underground expedition?\nIf they weren't here, there'd be no tunnels at all. It seems to make sense.\nThankfully, we found it first. So it's up to us to make the next move.
column6: 不然你要怎么解释那场庞大的地下勘探？\n要不是他们在这儿，根本不会有那些隧道。这似乎说得通。\n还好是我们先发现了它。所以下一步得由我们来走。

column5: I can't think of any other explanation, to be honest. So I'm definitely certain.\nThe Occupation of Mazeo was just a front for their true goal — the Idol.\nHowever certain I am of that, I'm still clueless as to {i}why{/i} they'd want it.
column6: 说实话我想不出别的解释。所以我非常确定。\n占领马泽奥只是他们真实目标的幌子——灵像。\n可我虽然对此深信不疑，却还是完全不明白他们{i}为什么{/i}想要它。

column5: We had a deal in place with the owner of Mazeo's Tavern.\nIt's not unlike Peregrino, actually. Almost existing as a front.\nBut he didn't want to get caught, since things were coming to a head.
column6: 我们和马泽奥酒馆的老板有过约定。\n其实跟佩雷格里诺差不多，几乎就是个幌子。\n但他不想被抓到，因为局势正走向白热化。

column5: So we decided to branch off, and find ourselves a new home.\nThat's when Damek set his eyes on the underground tunnels.\nHe'd been going to them for a while, to gather his mind in peace.
column6: 所以我们决定另起炉灶，给自己找个新家。\n就在这时，达梅克看中了那些地下隧道。\n他之前就常去那里，安静地整理思绪。

column5: Nobody. That's what made The Occupation such a good excuse.\nBefore they took over, it was a \"no man's land\". Everybody was free.\nThat had both upsides {i}and{/i} downsides, so they capitalized on the downsides.
column6: 没有人。正因如此，占领才成了个绝佳的借口。\n他们接管之前，这里是片“无主之地”，人人都自由自在。\n这既有好处{i}也{/i}有坏处，于是他们便拿坏处做文章。

column5: They promised the people a better future, and they just ate it up.\nFast-forward over twenty years, and they're starting to realize it was a lie.\nIt's helped us get some last minute recruits, but we can't count on any more of those.
column6: 他们向民众许诺了更好的未来，大家却全盘照信。\n一晃二十多年过去，人们开始意识到那是个谎言。\n这让我们在最后关头招到了一些人，但再指望更多就不可能了。

column5: Honestly, I'm not sure. We need to think about that when the war is over.\nWe could revert it to the way things were, or come up with a new form of government.\nI'm sure that whatever happens, though, we can't fully eliminate piracy.
column6: 老实说，我也不确定。等战争结束再考虑吧。\n我们可以恢复原样，也可以设计一种新的政体。\n但无论怎样，我都确信我们无法彻底根除海盗。

column5: Even if we lifted all trading bans, they'd just continue business as normal.\nThat's what my advice would be. We should legitimize them, put them to work.\nIt's easy to punish them, but there's a whole industry we could tap into.
column6: 就算我们解除所有贸易禁令，他们照样会照常做生意。\n我的建议就是这样。我们应该让他们合法化，让他们干活。\n惩罚他们很容易，但有一整个产业可供我们利用。

column5: There are two pirate lords, Alex and Nada.\nThey see eye to eye on most things, but disagree on others.\nStill, rather than fight each other, they've come to rule together.
column6: 有两位海盗头目，亚历克斯和娜达。\n他们在多数事情上看法一致，但也有分歧。\n不过他们没有彼此争斗，而是选择了共同统治。

column5: Some pirates prefer Alex, while others prefer Nada. It's not too complicated.\nBut there's enough drama around piracy to deal with in-fighting. So they work together.
column6: 有些海盗偏向亚历克斯，有些偏向娜达。倒也不难理解。\n但海盗营生本就风波不断，再内斗就应付不来了。所以他们联手合作。

column5: Piracy wasn't his first choice — but he really didn't have any say in the matter.\nNone of the legitimate trading companies would hire him due to his troubled past.\nHe basically takes whatever job he can get, living off of Nada's scraps.
column6: 当海盗并非他的首选——可这事根本由不得他。\n因为他那段糟糕的过去，正规的贸易商行没一家肯雇他。\n他基本上有什么活就接什么活，靠娜达的残羹剩饭过活。

column5: A lot of the local pirates follow after his ideals. He doesn't have delusions of grandeur.\nThe goods he smuggles aren't too dangerous either. It's pretty close to an honest living.\nHe just wants the trade bans lifted — to continue doing what he's doing, and be accepted.
column6: 本地不少海盗都追随他的理念。他没有那种狂妄自大的幻想。\n他走私的货物也不算太危险，几乎称得上正当营生。\n他只想让贸易禁令解除——好继续做自己的生意，并被认可。

column5: Now she's a different story entirely — nothing is off limits for her. She wants money, and power.\nAs long as the price is right, it doesn't matter what you want to smuggle. She's your girl.\nHer vision of the future is different than Alex's. One day, she sees herself in charge of Mazeo.
column6: 至于她，那就完全是另一回事了——对她来说没什么是禁忌。她要的是金钱和权力。\n只要价钱合适，你想走私什么都无所谓，找她就对了。\n她对未来的设想和亚历克斯不同。总有一天，她觉得自己会掌管马泽奥。

column5: A lot of the pirates follow her because she promises them riches and power. Alex doesn't do that.\nHe simply promises them a stable living, with the hopes that one day it's made legal.\nBut Nada doesn't care what's right or what's wrong, only about having the most power.
column6: 很多海盗追随她，因为她许诺财富和权力。亚历克斯则不会这么做。\n他只承诺安稳的生计，并希望有朝一日能让它合法化。\n可娜达不在乎什么对错，只在乎拥有最大的权力。

column5: I guess she thinks that if you have power, it doesn't matter {i}what{/i} you do.\nWhile Alex wants to live an honest legal life, Nada wants to be strong enough to do anything.\nIf you have the whole world in your hand — much like The Triumvirate — no one will stop you.
column6: 我猜她认为只要有权力，你做{i}什么{/i}都无所谓。\n亚历克斯想过一种正派合法的人生，娜达却想强大到无所不能。\n当你把整个世界握在手里——就像三人执政团那样——就没人能阻拦你。

column5: I've never had to think about it, so I don't really have an answer.\nBut I'd probably have to go with Alex. Nada is a bit too ruthless for me.\nIf she was in power, people would be under her thumb — rather than free.
column6: 我从没想过这个问题，所以真没什么答案。\n不过大概我会选亚历克斯。娜达对我来说太狠了些。\n要是她掌权，人们就都得受她摆布——而不是自由。

column5: Not really. Our previous leader ensured that we stayed well hidden.\nNot many of the townspeople knew what we were doing.\nBut even if they found out? They sided with us anyway.
column6: 不怎么会。我们前任领袖确保我们藏得很隐蔽。\n镇上没多少人知道我们在做什么。\n就算他们发现了呢？他们照样站在我们这边。

column5: His name was Salus, and he was a man of pure genius.\nI know we say that Damek is a good strategist, but Salus? He was incredible.\nIf it weren't for him, you wouldn't even be wearing that blade on your back.
column6: 他叫萨卢斯，是个不折不扣的天才。\n我知道我们都说达梅克是个出色的战略家，可萨卢斯？他简直不可思议。\n要不是他，你背上根本不会背着那把刃。

column5: To be honest, if we win this war — it'll all be thanks to him.\nWe have some work ahead of us, but he made it all possible.\nNot to discredit what you need to do, of course; but you get the idea.
column6: 说实话，要是我们赢了这场战争——全都得归功于他。\n前面还有不少事要做，但一切都是他铺好的路。\n当然，这不是要抹杀你要做的事，但你能明白我的意思。

column5: It's not that hard to be secretive, especially when you have to be.\nWe never slipped up, precisely because we couldn't {i}afford{/i} to.\nIt's also a bit easier with your key players hiding behind positions of power.
column6: 保密没那么难，尤其是在你不得不保密的时候。\n我们从未出过纰漏，正是因为出不起{i}任何{/i}纰漏。\n要是关键人物藏在有权有势的位置背后，那就更容易了。

column5: By that — I mean, nobody would question Gryz, or The Elder of Valinorth.\nSo because of that, him and Salus were able to meet and plan things without suspicion.\nEssentially, we had the perfect cover. After Salus passed, we just exercised discretion.
column6: 我的意思是，没人会去质疑格瑞兹，或是瓦利诺斯的长老。\n正因如此，他和萨卢斯才能在不被怀疑的情况下会面、谋划。\n可以说，我们有最完美的掩护。萨卢斯去世后，我们就更加谨慎行事了。

column5: Yes.
column6: 是的。

column5: With the knowledge I currently possess, yes, I think they would.\nOver twenty years later, the Mazeans are starting to realize The Triumvirate was lying.\nThey promised to turn Mazeo into a utopia. Just look around when we get there. It's not.
column6: 以我目前所知，是的，我想他们会。\n二十多年过去，马泽奥人开始意识到三人执政团一直在撒谎。\n他们许诺把马泽奥变成乌托邦。等我们到了你四处看看就知道，根本不是。

column5: Their words seem to mean a lot to people, even if their actions don't follow suit.\nIn my opinion, it's only a matter of time before their promises fall on deaf ears.\nThat is — if we don't take them down first. At least we'll be keeping {i}our{/i} promises.
column6: 他们的话对人们似乎很有分量，哪怕行动根本跟不上。\n在我看来，他们的承诺迟早会被人充耳不闻。\n也就是说——除非我们先把他们拉下马。至少我们会{i}兑现{/i}自己的承诺。

column5: Depends what you're wanting to know. Just give me a try.
column6: 那得看你想知道什么。尽管问吧。

column5: Old enough to be tired of answering that question.
column6: 老到已经懒得回答这个问题了。

column5: I consider Damek and The Rebellion to be my family.\nIf you mean my birth family in Alarinthia, I couldn't tell you.\nWe weren't very close, and I left for the mainland as soon as I could.
column6: 我把达梅克和反抗军当成家人。\n如果你指我在阿拉林西亚的血亲，那我可说不上来。\n我们关系并不亲近，我逮到机会就离开去了大陆。

column5: Depends how much you're paying me.
column6: 那得看你出多少钱。

column5: There isn't much to say. He always pops in to mess up our plans.\nEvery time we battle The Honor Guard, he's right there with them.\nThe Triumvirate barely leaves their castle, so he's almost like a stand-in for them.
column6: 没什么好说的。他总冒出来打乱我们的计划。\n每次我们和荣誉卫队交战时，他都和他们在一起。\n三人执政团几乎不离开他们的城堡，所以他差不多就是他们的替身。

column5: Basically, anytime we're against enemy forces, he's there.\nBut you learn a lot about the man in the way he fights. So I know a lot about him.\nI've never seen anybody with such strong conviction. He truly believes he's doing the right thing.
column6: 基本上，只要我们对抗敌军，他就在场。\n但从一个人的打法里能看出很多。所以我对他了解不少。\n我从没见过信念如此坚定的人。他真的相信自己做的没错。

column5: No, and I think I'd like to keep it that way.
column6: 没有，而且我希望一直如此。

column5: Forgive me if I ask you to be more specific.
column6: 请原谅，我得请你问得具体些。

column5: I haven't been able to get a read on her yet, which is rare for me.\nNormally I'm a good judge of character — but on her, I'm drawing a blank.\nNot to say that's a bad thing. She carries herself admirably; but she's just closed off.
column6: 我到现在还看不透她，这对我来说很少见。\n平时我挺会看人的——可对她，我一片空白。\n倒不是说这是坏事。她举止令人钦佩，只是太封闭了。

column5: At the end of the day, she won't cause me any concern, so that's a good thing.\nBut I find myself wondering why she's so scared to open up. It's not like we'll hurt her.\nSome might say that's a personality trait on its own, but not me. I like to dig deeper.
column6: 说到底，她不会让我操心，这是好事。\n可我忍不住想，她为什么这么怕敞开心扉。我们又不会伤害她。\n有人也许会说这本身就是种性格，但我不这么看。我喜欢往深处挖。

column5: Honestly? He's a little much. Energy wise, I mean.\nI used to be like him when I was younger, but it's better to conserve your energy.\nIf you waste it without thought like he does, you won't have it when you actually need it.
column6: 说实话？他有点太过了。我是说精力方面。\n我年轻时也像他那样，但还是节省点精力为好。\n要是像他那样不加思索地耗光，真需要的时候就没得用了。

column5: That's pretty much why I'm so calm all the time. I'm waiting to put my energy to good use.\nNormally, that \"good use\" involves either a fight, or some stiff drinks. You'll see.\nOnce we get to Mazeo, there's a Tavern that gets my highest recommendation.
column6: 这差不多就是我一直这么冷静的原因。我在等一个把精力用在刀刃上的机会。\n通常这种“刀刃”要么是打一架，要么是几杯烈酒。你会见识到的。\n等我们到了马泽奥，有家酒馆我极力推荐。

column5: We don't seem to get along, but he's actually one of my best friends.\nHe just has this way of poking fun at everybody. It's his way of showing love.\nWith a troubled past like his, I wouldn't be surprised if he thought that's what love {i}is{/i}.
column6: 我们看着合不来，可他其实是我最好的朋友之一。\n他就是有那种爱拿人打趣的毛病，那是他表达关爱的方式。\n有他那样坎坷的过去，他会以为爱{i}就是{/i}那样，我一点也不意外。

column5: You're good at following orders, I'll give you that much.\nI'm not sure if you're just clueless, or full of national pride.\nEither way, it's a good thing. We can't have you full of doubt.
column6: 你很听命令，这点我承认。\n我说不准你是真不懂，还是满怀家国自豪感。\n不管怎样，这都是好事。我们不能让你满心疑虑。

column5: It won't be much longer until you can kick back and relax.\nBut when you do, it'll be as Alestia's hero. Think about that.\nYou had a life of luxury just thrown into your lap. I'm jealous.
column6: 用不了多久，你就能彻底放松下来了。\n但到那时，你会是以阿莱斯蒂亚英雄的身份。好好想想吧。\n锦衣玉食的生活就这么砸到你怀里。我都有点羡慕。

column5: Well, spare time is pretty scarce these days. But I love a good drink.\nNothing better than winding down a busy day with some ale, right?\nAside from that, I love a good spar. But it's hard to find a challenge.
column6: 唉，这些天闲工夫少得可怜。不过我很爱喝一杯。\n忙完一天来点麦酒放松放松，没什么比这更好了，对吧？\n除此之外，我还喜欢痛快地切磋一场。只是很难找到对手。

column5: I'm not picky. I just like the effects.\nThe stronger stuff is more expensive though, and I'm not loaded.\nWell, unless Damek decides to treat me, I guess. That's rare, though.
column6: 我不挑，只要有效果就行。\n不过烈酒更贵，而我没什么钱。\n唔，除非达梅克肯请我，大概。不过那可少见。

column5: There's a huge Tavern tucked away in the Town Square. \nBest drinks money can buy, and like Peregrino, they have private rooms.\nGreat business model, actually. When you've had too much, they can con you into a room.
column6: 城广场里藏着一家大酒馆。\n那里有花钱能买到的最好的酒，而且跟佩雷格里诺一样有雅间。\n这生意经其实挺高明。等你喝多了，他们就能哄你开个房间。

column5: I'll point it out if I can. Might be a good idea to grab a drink before your training.\nDamek has a strict regiment set out for you, but I'll make sure you have fun. Don't worry.
column6: 有机会我会指给你看。训练前先去喝一杯也许不错。\n达梅克给你定了套严格的训练计划，不过我会保证让你玩得开心，别担心。

column5: Heh, of course. Now you're starting to grow on me.\nI didn't know you were into that, but I need a good drinking buddy.\nYou can only drink so much alone before it starts to get sad.
column6: 嘿，那当然。我开始有点喜欢你了。\n没想到你也好这口，我正缺个靠谱的酒友。\n一个人喝到一定程度就只剩下凄凉了。

column5: Yes.
column6: 是的。

column5: Wow! Mazeo looks so big, even from this far away!\nIt's easily five times bigger than Valinorth...!
column6: 哇！马泽奥从这么远看都好大！\n至少有瓦利诺斯的五倍大……！

column5: Try for ten, little one.\nJust stick by my side, and you won't get lost.\nI don't feel like running around town trying to find you.
column6: 往十倍上猜吧，小家伙。\n跟紧我身边就不会走丢。\n我可不想满城跑着找你。

column5: Again, I'm not little!\nAnd trust me, I'll never get lost.\nI have a pretty good sense of direction.
column6: 再说一遍，我不是小家伙！\n而且相信我，我绝不会走丢。\n我方向感很好的。

column5: Says the guy who got lost on his way home last week.
column6: 上周回家路上走丢的人是谁来着。

column5: Valessa, it was {i}dark{/i}!\nYou'd have done the same thing in my situation.
column6: 瓦莱莎，当时天{i}黑{/i}了！\n换你在我那个情况下也会一样的。

column5: Not true. I was home a few hours before you.\nJust take Ulric up on his offer Fortaime, he's being nice.\nWho knows what the pirates would do to you if they found you alone.
column6: 才不是。我比你早到家好几个小时。\n福泰姆，就接受乌尔里克的好意吧，他是在对你好。\n谁知道海盗要是发现你落单会干出什么来。

column5: Okay, and now you're scaring me.
column6: 好吧，你现在吓到我了。

column5: As Alex left his office, Gryz sat in contemplation.{w}\nIt wasn't long before Lillith, his assistant, walked into the room.{w}\nIt was her duty to document and follow-up with Gryz after every meeting.
column6: 亚历克斯离开办公室后，格瑞兹坐在那里沉思。{w}\n没过多久，他的助理莉莉丝走进了房间。{w}\n每次会谈后，记录并跟进格瑞兹的事务是她的职责。

column5: So, how'd it go?
column6: 那么，进展如何？

column5: As good as it could've, which isn't saying much.
column6: 能多顺利就多顺利吧，不过也就那样。

column5: What would you have me put on the record?
column6: 你要我在记录里写些什么？

column5: \"Negotiations to resume with more parties present.\"\nI think that about sums it up, while I gather my bearings.
column6: “更多方在场后重启谈判。”\n我想这就概括得差不多了，我也好理理头绪。

column5: Very well; and what about \"off the record\"?\nWhat should I be expecting to come through that door?
column6: 很好；那“不记录在案”的部分呢？\n我该期待什么人从那扇门里进来？

column5: Initially I wanted them to sabotage The Triumvirate's ships.\nBut that was very shortsighted of me. We'll need a naval army.\nSo I tackled things from another angle. Securing ships.
column6: 起初我想让他们去破坏三人执政团的船。\n但那想法太短视了。我们需要一支海军。\n所以我换了个角度下手：弄到船。

column5: That shouldn't be too hard, right?\nThe pirates have an enormous army.
column6: 那应该不难吧？\n海盗的兵力可不少。

column5: Combined, yeah. But I can't win them all over.\nAlex and Nada will both be fighting to cut a deal with me.\nAnd I'm afraid no matter who we side with, things will change.
column6: 合起来算，是不难。可我没法把他们全都争取过来。\n亚历克斯和娜达都会争着跟我达成协议。\n而恐怕不管我们站哪边，局面都会发生变化。

column5: For who, exactly?
column6: 对谁而言？

column5: Everybody.\nLillith, can you send for Damek?\nHe'll need to be present at the final negotiations.
column6: 所有人。\n莉莉丝，能派人去叫达梅克吗？\n最终谈判他得在场。

column5: Of course, sir.
column6: 当然，先生。

column5: I have a feeling he'll be bringing The Seer too, Lillith.\nWith everybody under one roof, we can finally make some progress.\nAt the end of the day, Mazeo and The Rebellion will be allied with the pirates.
column6: 莉莉丝，我感觉他还会把先知带来。\n所有人都聚到一处，我们终于能有进展了。\n说到底，马泽奥和反抗军将与海盗结盟。

column5: Never thought I'd see the day.\nI guess we just have to choose {i}who{/i} to side with.
column6: 没想到还能看到这一天。\n看来我们只需决定该站{i}哪一边{/i}。

column5: That's why I need to see Damek as well.\nHe'll be leading the final battle, so he needs to choose.\nI trust his decision, and his sense of strategy, more than you know.
column6: 所以我得见达梅克。\n最终一战将由他指挥，所以这个选择得他来做。\n我对他的决断和战略眼光的信任，超乎你所知。

column5: Should he really be making choices that affect the future of Mazeo?
column6: 真该由他来做影响马泽奥未来的决定吗？

column5: I think it's in our best interest.\nBesides, with what's coming, I don't think I'll be here much longer.\nI only hope that we can leave behind a peaceful future for Mazeo...
column6: 我觉得这样对我们最有利。\n再说，照这形势发展下去，我想我在这儿也待不久了。\n我只希望我们能给马泽奥留下一个和平的未来……

column5: As we take our first steps into Mazeo, we all pause and examine the surroundings.{w}\nIt's a crowded mess, with people running in every conceivable direction.{w} \nMarket stalls are set up wherever there's room — with all sorts of wares.
column6: 我们刚踏进马泽奥，就都停下脚步打量四周。{w}\n这里拥挤杂乱，人们朝着四面八方奔走。{w} \n凡是有空的地方就支着摊子——摆满各式各样的货品。

column5: Wait — I think I see them!
column6: 等等——我好像看到他们了！

column5: Fortaime immediately tries running ahead, enthralled by something he sees.{w}\nBut before he can get very far, Ulric grabs him from behind and stops him.{w}\nWith a tight grip on Fortaime's collar, it's clear he's not going anywhere.
column6: 福泰姆立刻想往前跑，被眼前的什么东西迷住了。{w}\n可他还没跑出几步，乌尔里克就从身后一把抓住了他。{w}\n乌尔里克死死攥着福泰姆的衣领，显然他哪儿也去不了。

column5: H-hey! What gives!?
column6: 喂、喂！干嘛啊！？

column5: You can't just run off into a crowd like that, Fortaime.\nYou'll get lost; and I don't have the time to find you.\nStick close to us, we'll get over there eventually.
column6: 你不能就这么一头扎进人堆里，福泰姆。\n你会走丢的，而我没时间去找你。\n跟紧我们，我们总会过去的。

column5: Alright...
column6: 好吧……

column5: His ears droop down, and he starts to mope around.{w}\nBut before he gets too sad, Ulric reaches into his pockets.{w}\nPulling out some coin, he gives it to Fortaime with a smile.
column6: 他的耳朵耷拉下来，开始闷闷不乐地晃悠。{w}\n还没等他太难过，乌尔里克把手伸进口袋。{w}\n他掏出几枚硬币，笑着递给福泰姆。

column5: Here's some money to spend on whatever you want.\nBut like I said — just make sure you stick close to us.\nThis isn't the kind of place you want to be alone in.
column6: 这些钱给你，想买什么就买什么。\n不过我说过了——一定得跟紧我们。\n这地方可不适合一个人待着。

column5: Wow, thanks Ulric!\nI'm gonna look for some apples, then.\nCan you point them out for me so I don't get lost?
column6: 哇，谢谢你，乌尔里克！\n那我去找点苹果。\n你能指给我看吗，免得我走丢？

column5: Yeah, they should be over there.
column6: 嗯，应该就在那边。

column5: Pointing to a nearby market stall, Fortaime runs off, jubilant.{w}\nFree money from Ulric? He must've taken a liking to Fortaime.{w}\nEither that, or he figured somebody needed to keep him in line.
column6: 乌尔里克指向附近的一个摊位，福泰姆欢天喜地地跑开了。{w}\n乌尔里克白白给钱？他肯定是喜欢上福泰姆了。{w}\n要不然，就是他觉得总得有个人管着他。

column5: Well, I guess we should keep an eye out for Damek.\nKnowing him, he's already here waiting for us.\nDo you see him anywhere, Pro?
column6: 好吧，我们该留意一下达梅克了。\n以他的性子，他早就在这儿等我们了。\n普洛，你看到他了吗？

column5: There's too many people.\nGive me a few minutes, I'll find him.
column6: 人太多了。\n给我几分钟，我去找他。

column5: A few moments later, Fortaime returns.{w}\nHe's holding an apple, his eyes glistening with happiness.
column6: 片刻之后，福泰姆回来了。{w}\n他手里握着一个苹果，眼里闪着幸福的光。

column5: Look, I finally got what I wanted!\nIt was so expensive though — I only had enough for one.\nI guess I'll have to make it last as long as possible, huh...?
column6: 看，我终于买到想要的了！\n不过太贵了——我的钱只够买一个。\n看来我得让它撑得越久越好，是吧……？

column5: Only one...?\nYou were conned, Fortaime.\nI should've followed you after all.
column6: 才一个……？\n你被坑了，福泰姆。\n我终究还是该跟着你的。

column5: Conned?
column6: 被坑？

column5: Yeah — taken advantage of.\nThe locals know a tourist when they see one.\nThey raise the prices because you don't know any better.
column6: 是啊——被人占了便宜。\n本地人一眼就能认出游客。\n看你什么都不懂，他们就抬价。

column5: Mean...!
column6: 好过份……！

column5: Sorry, it's my fault.\nFor a moment, I put too much faith in the people.\nAt least now you know all of my warnings were true.
column6: 抱歉，是我的错。\n有那么一瞬间，我对这些人太过信任了。\n至少现在你知道我那些警告都是真的了。

column5: Ulric lets out a large sigh, and continues scouting the surroundings.{w}\nHe takes a few steps in different directions, as if that helped his search.{w}\nBut Valessa calls out to us shortly after, pointing back towards the gate.
column6: 乌尔里克长叹一口气，继续在周围搜寻。{w}\n他朝几个方向各走了几步，好像这样就能找到似的。{w}\n但没过多久，瓦莱莎喊住我们，手指向城门那边。

column5: Is that him...?
column6: 那是他吗……？

column5: A man that was standing there starts to laugh and approach us.{w}\nHe was standing with his back against the gate — out of sight.{w}\nIt was a perfect hiding spot, since we'd be looking ahead.
column6: 站在那边的一个男人笑了起来，朝我们走来。{w}\n他一直背靠着城门站着——正好在视线之外。{w}\n那是个绝佳的藏身处，因为我们的目光都朝前看。

column5: I just wanted to see if you'd notice me, actually.\nYou've got a good eye on you. Valessa, right?
column6: 其实我只是想看看你们会不会注意到我。\n你眼力不错。瓦莱莎，对吧？

column5: Yeah — The Elder of Valinorth.\nPleased to meet you, Damek, sir.\nYour friends have really talked you up.
column6: 是的——瓦利诺斯的长老。\n幸会，达梅克先生。\n你的朋友们可把你夸上天了。

column5: And I'm Fortaime, The Scribe!\nWe've heard a lot about you, actually.
column6: 我是福泰姆，书记官！\n其实我们听过很多关于你的事。

column5: Yeah — Valinorth's Scribe.\nPleased to meet you, Damek.
column6: 是的——瓦利诺斯的书记官。\n幸会，达梅克。

column5: And I'm Fortaime, The Elder!\nWe've heard a lot about you, actually.
column6: 我是福泰姆，长老！\n其实我们听过很多关于你的事。

column5: All nonsense, I'm sure.
column6: 肯定都是些胡扯。

column5: After smiling at Valessa and Fortaime, he approaches me.
column6: 他朝瓦莱莎和福泰姆笑了笑，随后走向我。

column5: And you must be [firstname].\nIt feels like I've been waiting forever to meet you.\nHonestly, the last little while has been so hectic.
column6: 那你一定就是[firstname]了。\n感觉我已经等了好久好久，就为了见你一面。\n说实话，最近这段时间实在太忙乱了。

column5: And you must be [firstname].\nIt feels like I've been waiting forever to meet you.\nHonestly, the last little while has been so hectic.
column6: 那你一定就是[firstname]了。\n感觉我已经等了好久好久，就为了见你一面。\n说实话，最近这段时间实在太忙乱了。

column5: He blushes, and I can tell he's extremely nervous.{w}\nIt's odd — because he greeted Valessa and Fortaime with ease.{w}\nIt humbles me to see a man of such importance treat me this way.
column6: 他脸红了，看得出他极其紧张。{w}\n这很奇怪——因为他刚才和瓦莱莎、福泰姆打招呼时那么从容。{w}\n看到这样一位大人物如此待我，我不禁心生谦卑。

column5: I almost can't believe this is happening.\nIt's an honor to meet you, [firstname] — it truly is.
column6: 我几乎不敢相信这是真的。\n能见到你实在是我的荣幸，[firstname]——真的。

column5: I almost can't believe this is happening.\nIt's an honor to meet you, [firstname] — it truly is.
column6: 我几乎不敢相信这是真的。\n能见到你实在是我的荣幸，[firstname]——真的。

column5: What...? Oh, cut it out.\nThere's no need to say things like that.\nTrust me — you're already on my good side.
column6: 什么……？哦，别这么说。\n没必要讲这种话。\n相信我——你早就是我心目中的好人选了。

column5: I reach out to shake his hand, but he immediately pulls back.{w}\nWith a nervous laugh, he rubs the back of his head. Did I do something wrong?{w}\nHe seemed excited to meet me, so I assumed a handshake was in order.
column6: 我伸手想和他握手，他却立刻缩了回去。{w}\n他紧张地笑了笑，挠着后脑勺。我做错什么了吗？{w}\n他看起来见到我很兴奋，所以我还以为该握个手。

column5: And you're just as polite as I imagined!\nThere's no need to be so formal. You're among friends.
column6: 你果然和我想象中一样有礼！\n不用这么拘谨，这里都是自己人。

column5: I reach out to shake his hand, but he immediately pulls back.{w}\nWith a nervous laugh, he rubs the back of his head. Did I do something wrong?{w}\nHe seemed excited to meet me, so I assumed a handshake was in order.
column6: 我伸手想和他握手，他却立刻缩了回去。{w}\n他紧张地笑了笑，挠着后脑勺。我做错什么了吗？{w}\n他看起来见到我很兴奋，所以我还以为该握个手。

column5: You're joking, right...?\nI think the spirits themselves have chosen you.\nIn my mind — there's no greater honor than that.
column6: 你在开玩笑吧……？\n我认为是灵亲自选择了你。\n在我看来——没有比这更高的荣耀了。

column5: As a formality, I reach out to shake his hand, but he immediately pulls back.{w}\nWith a nervous laugh, he rubs the back of his head. Did I do something wrong?{w}\nHe seemed excited to meet me, so I assumed a handshake was in order.
column6: 出于礼节，我伸手想和他握手，他却立刻缩了回去。{w}\n他紧张地笑了笑，挠着后脑勺。我做错什么了吗？{w}\n他看起来见到我很兴奋，所以我还以为该握个手。

column5: I hope the journey from Valinorth wasn't too bad.\nThe weather seemed fair. It's just those Bloodleaves...\nWe might have to talk about that some more in a bit.
column6: 希望从瓦利诺斯来的旅途不算太糟。\n天气看着还不错。就是那些血叶……\n我们待会儿也许得再谈谈这件事。

column5: I reach out to shake his hand, but he immediately pulls back.{w}\nWith a nervous laugh, he rubs the back of his head. Did I do something wrong?{w}\nHe seemed excited to meet me, so I assumed a handshake was in order.
column6: 我伸手想和他握手，他却立刻缩了回去。{w}\n他紧张地笑了笑，挠着后脑勺。我做错什么了吗？{w}\n他看起来见到我很兴奋，所以我还以为该握个手。

column5: Anyway — shall we get going...?\nWe have quite a busy day ahead of us.
column6: 总之——我们出发吧？\n今天要忙的事可不少。

column5: He starts walking, expecting us to follow.{w}\nBut as soon as he gets to Pro, he stops in his tracks.
column6: 他开始往前走，等着我们跟上。{w}\n可一走到普洛面前，他就停住了脚步。

column5: Oh, just one more thing before we move along.\nYou'll be on cleaning duty for the next month, Pro.
column6: 哦，走之前还有一件事。\n普洛，接下来一个月你负责打扫。

column5: What!? What did I do...?
column6: 什么！？我做了什么……？

column5: It's more about what you {i}didn't{/i} do.\nAnd the answer to that — is everything.\nI ended up sending Ulric to pick up your slack.
column6: 更准确地说，是你{i}没做{/i}什么。\n而答案是——什么都没做。\n最后我只好派乌尔里克去补你的缺。

column5: We can't afford to waste time anymore.\nI'm sure you had your reasons, but—
column6: 我们再也耗不起时间了。\n我相信你有你的理由，可是——

column5: Yeah, and they were really good reasons!\nI couldn't just march into Valinorth with the blade!\nI need to have {i}some{/i} discretion. It took time!
column6: 是啊，而且都是非常充分的理由！\n我总不能背着那把刃大摇大摆走进瓦利诺斯吧！\n我总得有点{i}分寸{/i}。这需要时间！

column5: Really, Pro?\nYou know you can't throw excuses at me.\nI know how this stuff works. You were lazy.
column6: 真的吗，普洛？\n你知道你糊弄不了我。\n这种事我清楚得很。你就是偷懒了。

column5: He lets out a loud sigh, while Pro shuffles in place, ashamed.
column6: 他长叹一声，普洛则羞愧地原地挪着脚。

column5: I suppose it's my fault in the first place.\nI should've known better than to send you there.\nWith a Tavern in the way, your priorities would be clear.
column6: 说起来，这起初也该怪我。\n我早该知道不该派你去那种地方。\n有家酒馆挡在路上，你的优先级可想而知。

column5: After their spat, Damek turns to face me with a smile.\nEven when he was scolding — it was polite. That's interesting.\nI can start to see why people would like to follow him.
column6: 两人斗完嘴，达梅克笑着转向我。\n就连训人的时候，他也彬彬有礼。这挺有意思。\n我开始明白为什么人们愿意追随他了。

column5: Anyway, we have some business with The Mayor.\nLet's head to his house — I'll explain there.\nAfter that, I'll give you a tour of our HQ.
column6: 总之，我们和市长有些事要谈。\n去他家吧——我到那儿再解释。\n之后我带你们参观一下我们的总部。

column5: Plans with Gryz...?\nIs it about the Pirates?
column6: 和格瑞兹的计划……？\n是关于海盗的事吗？

column5: I said I'd explain when we get there, Ulric.\nWe can't talk about this kinda stuff out in the open.\nFinish up whatever business you have, and we'll get going.
column6: 我说了到了再解释，乌尔里克。\n这种事不能在大庭广众下谈。\n把手头的事办完，我们就出发。

column5: With that said, I guess it was time to head to The Mayor's house.{w}\nI knew nothing about Mazeo, so I didn't know if this was a detour or not.{w}\nBut either way, my training with The Blade of Exodus would surely begin today.
column6: 话虽如此，该去市长家了。{w}\n我对马泽奥一无所知，所以不知道这算不算绕路。{w}\n但无论如何，我的流亡之刃训练今天肯定要开始了。

column5: I look at Valessa and Fortaime, and we nod at one another.{w}\nI guess I'd finish up any business here, then follow Damek.{w}\nMy legs are tired — but it feels like our trek was almost over.
column6: 我看了看瓦莱莎和福泰姆，彼此点了点头。{w}\n我想，我得先办完这里的事，再跟达梅克走。{w}\n我的腿很累——但感觉这趟跋涉快到头了。

column5: Damek has now permanently joined your party.\nA new statistic, Morale, has also been unlocked.
column6: 达梅克现已永久加入你的队伍。\n新属性“士气”也已解锁。

column5: Morale may rise and fall over the course of the game.{w}\nYour army and their welfare will be affected by your choices.{w}\nEnsure a high Morale, or your forces may not survive the coming war.
column6: 士气会在游戏进程中起伏。{w}\n你的选择将影响你的军队及其福祉。{w}\n务必保持高士气，否则你的军队可能撑不过即将到来的战争。

column5: Hey.
column6: 嘿。

column5: Well, it all depends on what you'd like to know.\nI mean, I'm an open book, but I don't know where to start.\nFeel free to throw a few questions at me. I'll play along.
column6: 那得看你想知道什么了。\n我是说，我没什么好隐瞒的，可不知道该从哪儿说起。\n尽管问我几个问题，我会配合的。

column5: Twenty-seven. Not too young, not too old.\nI'm in the perfect place to be leading this army.\nA lot of the other victims were far younger than me.
column6: 二十七岁。不算太年轻，也不算太老。\n我正处在统领这支军队的最佳年纪。\n其他许多受害者都比我小得多。

column5: And those that weren't, were far older.\nThey took on more of a \"caregiver\" role.\nPlenty of orphans needed plenty of parents.
column6: 而那些不是的，都比我大得多。\n他们更多扮演着“看护者”的角色。\n那么多孤儿，需要那么多父母。

column5: I must've been about six or seven years old.\nA lot of the details are like a blur in my head.\nMaybe my mind did that on purpose, you know?
column6: 我那时大概只有六七岁。\n很多细节在我脑中都是一片模糊。\n也许是我的脑子故意如此，你懂吧？

column5: But I was rescued by a small group of townspeople.\nAfter the battle died down, they started picking up the scraps.\nThe Rebellion wasn't formed just yet, that was just starting.
column6: 不过我被一小群镇民救了下来。\n战斗平息后，他们开始收拾残局。\n那时候反抗军还没成立，才刚刚起步。

column5: Salus, the previous Elder of Valinorth, came to visit.\nThe treaty, and The Rebellion, were formed shortly after.\nI had no place to go, and no family. I was forced to fight.
column6: 瓦利诺斯的前任长老萨卢斯来探访。\n不久之后，条约和反抗军便成立了。\n我无处可去，也无家可归，只能被迫战斗。

column5: But that's not really a bad thing, you know?\nI'm pretty strong now, trained for almost any scenario.\nI just wish I didn't have to miss out on a regular childhood.
column6: 不过你知道，这其实也不算坏事。\n我现在挺强的，几乎什么情况都训练过。\n我只是希望自己不必错过一个正常的童年。

column5: Oh, of course not. I don't have time for that.\nI mean, maybe when this war is over, or something.\nBut right now? I'm far too busy with everything else.
column6: 哦，当然没有。我没那个时间。\n我是说，也许等这场战争结束了什么的。\n但现在？别的事已经够我忙的了。

column5: And truth be told, I wouldn't even know where to start.\nThe orphans of the occupation were taught war, not love.\nOther than fighting this battle, I'm not meant for much else.
column6: 说实话，我甚至不知道该从何开始。\n占领时期的孤儿学到的是战争，而不是爱。\n除了打这场仗，我大概也做不了别的。

column5: I don't really have time for hobbies, to be honest.\nUnless the war table, or sparring, count as hobbies.\nAfter this war, maybe I'll pick up a few pastimes.
column6: 老实说，我没什么时间发展爱好。\n除非作战桌和切磋也算爱好。\n等这场战争结束，也许我会找几个消遣。

column5: But right now, I really don't have the time.\nI've been training and working since I was a kid.\nThey had no hesitation in letting a child wield a sword.
column6: 但现在，我真的没时间。\n我从小就在训练和工作。\n他们毫不犹豫地让一个孩子拿起剑。

column5: Well, almost everything, I'd assume.\nI was one of the \"founding members\" with Salus.\nI guess they liked that term more than \"child soldier\".
column6: 嗯，我想几乎所有事吧。\n我是和萨卢斯一起的“创始成员”之一。\n大概是他们觉得这说法比“童子军”好听。

column5: When The Triumvirate took over Mazeo, they had one goal.\nDig deep underground, and find the true spirit idol of this nation.\nThey made their Honor Guard do this. Those empty suits of armor.
column6: 三人执政团接管马泽奥时，只有一个目标。\n往地下深处挖掘，找到这个国家真正的灵像。\n他们让荣誉卫队来做这件事。就是那些空荡荡的盔甲。

column5: But while they dug, they also created a sort of \"barracks\" down there.\nI'm not sure why, because the Honor Guard couldn't make use of it.\nBut I'm assuming it was for when real people came for inspections.
column6: 但挖掘的同时，他们也在下面建了个类似“营房”的地方。\n我不清楚为什么，因为荣誉卫队根本用不上。\n不过我猜那是给真人来视察时用的。

column5: Either way, they basically turned it into a paradise.\nBeds, weapons, training rooms, a war table — everything.\nWhen I first saw it, I knew I had to win it for The Rebellion.
column6: 不管怎样，他们基本上把它打造成了一个天堂。\n床铺、武器、训练室、作战桌——应有尽有。\n我第一次看到时，就知道必须为反抗军把它夺过来。

column5: Thankfully, Gryz had been turning to our side.\nIt wasn't hard to woo over The Mayor, and get the deed.\nHis only condition was that {i}he{/i} got access to the idol first.
column6: 还好，格瑞兹当时已经在倒向我们。\n拉拢市长、拿到地契并不难。\n他唯一的条件就是{i}他{/i}要先接触那尊灵像。

column5: I'm not sure what he wants to do with it.\nBut he can't really do anything, if I'm honest.\nNot without you, or The Blade of Exodus.
column6: 我不清楚他想拿它做什么。\n但说实话，他也做不了什么。\n没有你，或是没有流亡之刃，他都办不到。

column5: Salus? Well, he was a father figure to a lot of us.\nThat's probably why his sacrifice hit us all so hard.\nYou {i}do{/i} remember that he was The Elder of Valinorth, right?
column6: 萨卢斯？他就像我们许多人的父亲。\n大概正因如此，他的牺牲才让我们所有人深受打击。\n你{i}应该{/i}记得他是瓦利诺斯的长老吧？

column5: It's not like he took on a secret double life, he was still the same.\nIf anything, at least now you have an explanation for his \"trips\".\nHe was helping out The Rebellion {i}and{/i} Valinorth. That's a tall order.
column6: 他并不是过起了什么秘密的双面人生，他还是原来那个他。\n要说有什么不同，至少现在你能解释他的那些“外出”了。\n他同时帮着反抗军{i}和{/i}瓦利诺斯。这可不是一般的担子。

column5: Salus saw the chaos and destruction in Mazeo, and wanted to help.\nIn fact, even some people from Valinorth were here during The Occupation.\nHe likely discovered what happened by inquiring after their \"disappearance\".
column6: 萨卢斯目睹了马泽奥的混乱与毁灭，想要伸出援手。\n其实，占领期间连一些瓦利诺斯人也在这里。\n他大概是通过打听他们的“失踪”才得知了事情的经过。

column5: Either way, he quickly met with the band of survivors and orphans.\nOffering them funding, and protection, the seeds were planted.\nThey became an organization, with a goal. They had purpose.
column6: 总之，他很快会见了那群幸存者和孤儿。\n提供资金和保护，种子就此埋下。\n他们成了一个有目标的组织，有了自己的使命。

column5: Salus likely knew that Valinorth would be occupied as well.\nSo training an army to enact revenge would benefit both nations.\nThey established Peregrino as a central location, and here we are.
column6: 萨卢斯大概料到瓦利诺斯也会被占领。\n所以训练一支军队去复仇对两个国家都有好处。\n他们把佩雷格里诺设为中枢，于是就有了今天。

column5: Over the next twenty years, the orphans grew stronger.\nAs soon as we were battle-ready, we launched the Exodus Raid.\nSalus told me more about {i}you{/i}, and I took over when he passed.
column6: 接下来的二十年里，孤儿们越来越强。\n我们一做好战斗准备，就发动了流亡突袭。\n萨卢斯跟我讲了更多关于{i}你{/i}的事，他去世后便由我接手。

column5: Several hundred, but under a thousand.\nWe're a fully realized army, and I {i}know{/i} we can do this.\nWith you and that blade, our victory is pretty much secured.
column6: 几百人，不到一千。\n我们是一支羽翼丰满的军队，我{i}知道{/i}我们做得到。\n有你，还有那把刃，我们的胜利几乎已经稳了。

column5: It's wonderful. Everybody is in a great mood.\nWe have the numbers, and the strength to put up a fight.\nBut on top of that, we have {i}you{/i}, and The Blade of Exodus.
column6: 非常好。每个人都斗志高昂。\n我们有兵力，也有抗衡的实力。\n而除此之外，我们还有{i}你{/i}，还有流亡之刃。

column5: When you're trained with it, you can lead the final battle.\nThat Blade isn't just a weapon — but a symbol of hope.\nIt sets us apart from every previous insurrection.
column6: 等你练成之后，就能领军打最后一战。\n那把刃不只是武器——更是希望的象征。\n它让我们与以往每一次起义都截然不同。

column5: With its power, you'll be unstoppable.\nI hope you're ready to go down in history as a hero.\nThe man who changed Alestia {i}forever{/i}.
column6: 有了它的力量，你将无可阻挡。\n希望你已准备好作为英雄载入史册。\n那个{i}永远{/i}改变了阿莱斯蒂亚的男人。

column5: With its power, you'll be unstoppable.\nI hope you're ready to go down in history as a hero.\nThe woman who changed Alestia {i}forever{/i}.
column6: 有了它的力量，你将无可阻挡。\n希望你已准备好作为英雄载入史册。\n那个{i}永远{/i}改变了阿莱斯蒂亚的女人。

column5: We don't know too much about them, to be honest.\nThey're shrouded in mystery, and only rule from their chambers.\nWe've tried to coax them out, but so far, nothing has worked.
column6: 老实说，我们对他们了解不多。\n他们笼罩在谜团之中，只在寝宫里发号施令。\n我们试过引他们出来，但至今毫无成效。

column5: Not a clue. It's anyone's guess.\nHopefully we'll find some answers after all this is over.\nThere's gotta be some record of their past, right?
column6: 一无所知。谁也说不准。\n希望等这一切结束后能找到些答案。\n他们的过去总该有些记录吧？

column5: At least, that's what I'm hoping for.\nBut I'll have to be content if we never find out.\nMy main goal is liberating Alestia, and gaining freedom.
column6: 至少我是这么希望的。\n但如果始终查不出来，我也只能接受。\n我的主要目标是解放阿莱斯蒂亚，赢得自由。

column5: At least as old as Alestia. Or something like that.\nHistory seems to have \"begun\" when they did.\nEither that, or they covered up the past.
column6: 至少和阿莱斯蒂亚一样古老，大概是这样。\n历史似乎是从他们出现时“开始”的。\n要么如此，要么就是他们掩盖了过去。

column5: There's no record of history prior to their rule.\nSo that's why everybody regards them as \"Gods\".\nBut there's more to the story, I can feel it in my gut.
column6: 他们统治之前的历史没有任何记录。\n所以人人都把他们奉为“神明”。\n但事情不止于此，我的直觉告诉我的。

column5: No, we just know that they wear white and gold cloaks.\nThis is from reliable firsthand accounts, of course.\nSome people have met them and lived to tell.
column6: 不，我们只知道他们披着白金色的斗篷。\n当然，这来自可靠的第一手证词。\n有人见过他们，还活着把这事说了出来。

column5: Underneath those cloaks, however, is anyone's guess.\nSome people even theorize that there's nothing underneath.\nThat's pretty scary, if you ask me. They'd be like living spirits.
column6: 至于斗篷底下是什么，谁也说不准。\n有人甚至推测底下什么都没有。\n要我来说，那可挺吓人的。他们就像活着的灵。

column5: I think so. As far as we know, they've had it forever.\nAncient writings and murals have depicted the blade.\nWe still don't know for sure, though. They could've found it.
column6: 我想是的。据我们所知，那把刃一直属于他们。\n古老的文字和壁画上都描绘过那把刃。\n不过我们还不能确定。也许他们是捡到的。

column5: What we need to worry about, is the power the blade houses.\nIt gave them the power to enslave an entire world of innocent people.\nWe must never resort to the same thing. I want to destroy it when this is over.
column6: 我们该担心的是那把刃蕴含的力量。\n它赋予了他们奴役这整个无辜世界的力量。\n我们绝不能重蹈覆辙。等这一切结束后，我想毁掉它。

column5: I'd like to think so, yeah.\nIt's actually a bit ironic, isn't it...?\nTheir own weapon, used against them.
column6: 我倒愿意这么想。\n其实还挺讽刺的，不是吗……？\n用他们自己的武器来对付他们。

column5: As soon as you learn to use it, we'll be good to go.\nI have no doubt in my mind that it's strong enough.\nYou were chosen by the spirits for this destiny.
column6: 等你学会使用它，我们就能行动了。\n我毫不怀疑它的力量足够强大。\n你是被灵选中来承担这份命运的。

column5: Sure, what would you like to know?
column6: 当然，你想知道什么？

column5: Well, I don't really know anything about her, yet.\nBut I'd like to change that, if I get the opportunity.\nI think she seems like a wonderful person.
column6: 嗯，我还不太了解她。\n但如果有机会，我想改变这一点。\n我觉得她看起来是个很好的人。

column5: He seems really... energetic?\nHonestly, you'll have to ask me again in the future.\nWe just haven't had the chance to hang out just yet.
column6: 他看起来真的很……有活力？\n老实说，这事你以后得再问我一次。\n我们到现在还没机会好好相处过。

column5: Ulric is one of my best friends. He really is.\nThere's no man I'd rather have at my back in battle.\nHe's saved me from dying more times than I can count.
column6: 乌尔里克是我最好的朋友之一。真的。\n战场上，我最想让他守在我身后。\n他救过我性命的次数我数都数不清。

column5: The Rebellion basically hinges on my planning, and his strength.\nHe'll be at the front of every charge, I can guarantee that much.\nThere's no man in this world quite as strong as him.
column6: 反抗军基本上就靠我的谋划和他的武力撑着。\n我敢保证，每次冲锋他都会在最前面。\n这世上没有哪个男人比他更强。

column5: Right now, I'm a little upset with him, but I'll manage.\nHe's my go-to man when something involves being \"sneaky\".\nHis reconnaissance work has been a great boon to our efforts.
column6: 眼下我对他有点不满，不过我能应付。\n凡是需要“偷偷摸摸”的事，我都找他。\n他的侦察工作对我们的行动帮助极大。

column5: I suspect that you'll be working with him closely in the future.\nA lot of our final attack on Balteus will involve a stealthy infiltration.\nBut we'll get to more of that in the future. So no need to waste time on it now.
column6: 我猜以后你会和他密切合作。\n我们对巴尔泰乌斯的最终进攻很大一部分要靠隐秘渗透。\n不过那些以后再细说，现在不必浪费时间。

column5: Well, I wouldn't know where to start. \nYou're such an important figure to both me and my army.\nBut to Alestia...? You're going to be known as their savior.
column6: 嗯，我都不知从何说起。\n对我和我的军队来说，你是如此重要的人物。\n但对阿莱斯蒂亚……？你会被当成他们的救世主。

column5: I have to admit, you're a bit different than I expected.\nAll this stuff had me thinking you'd be larger than life.\nBut I guess that's my fault. You're just a normal person.
column6: 我得承认，你和我想象中有点不一样。\n这些事让我以为你会是个传奇般的人物。\n不过这大概是我的错。你不过是个普通人。

column5: The thing that makes you special is on the inside, not the outside.\nI guess it just benefits us that not everybody can see that, right?\nWe wouldn't want you to be a walking target for the enemy to find.
column6: 让你与众不同的东西在内在，而不是外表。\n我觉得，不是人人都看得出来，这对我们反而是好事，对吧？\n我们可不想让你成为敌人眼里会走路的靶子。

column5: Sure. Anything specific...?
column6: 当然。有具体想问的吗……？

column5: Well, I'll have you rest for the day. \nThen we'll start training you with The Blade of Exodus tomorrow.\nI think that slow exposure therapy will be the best possible approach.
column6: 嗯，今天你先休息。\n明天我们就开始带你练流亡之刃。\n我觉得逐步接触的疗法是最好的办法。

column5: As you build a tolerance for its power, you'll be able to wield it longer.\nOf course, you'll also be training in the basics of sword play.\nUlric will make sure that you learn everything you need to.
column6: 随着你对它的力量逐渐产生耐受，你就能使用得更久。\n当然，你也会接受剑术基础训练。\n乌尔里克会确保你学会所有该学的。

column5: We have the benefit of foresight, here.\nWe know The Triumvirate will be busy with Valinorth.\nYou can train, and we can attack Balteus {i}right{/i} under their noses.
column6: 我们在这里占着先见之明。\n我们知道三人执政团会忙于瓦利诺斯。\n你可以安心训练，而我们可以{i}就{/i}在他们眼皮底下进攻巴尔泰乌斯。

column5: Yeah, and it's something you'll be hearing more of.\nWe have some stuff to take care of for now.\nYou'll get used to the war table, trust me.
column6: 是啊，以后你还会经常听到这说法。\n眼下我们还有些事要处理。\n你会习惯作战桌的，相信我。

column5: Probably in chaos, and disarray.\nWe can't expect the people to embrace the new leadership.\nBut we'll do our best to win them over, and cater to their desires.
column6: 大概会陷入混乱和动荡。\n我们不能指望民众会欣然接受新政权。\n但我们会尽力争取他们，并满足他们的诉求。

column5: Anything we learn about The Triumvirate will also be useful.\nIf we can prove that they're frauds, the people will accept us easier.\nThe only question is — how in the world do we go about doing that?
column6: 我们了解到的关于三人执政团的任何事都会有用。\n要是能证明他们是骗子，民众会更容易接受我们。\n唯一的问题是——我们到底要怎么做？

column5: Either way, we'll have lots of work ahead of us.\nWinning this battle doesn't mean we can sit back and rest.\nWe'll have an entire world to rule, and reform. I can't wait.
column6: 不管怎样，前头都有大量工作等着我们。\n赢下这场战斗并不意味着我们能高枕无忧。\n我们要统治并改革整个世界。我都等不及了。

column5: You mean imbue it with spiritual energy? I'm not sure.\nBut I wouldn't classify your nation as dead. Not just yet.\nThe power inside of you is proof that we can redirect it.
column6: 你是说给它注入灵性能量？我不确定。\n但我不会说你的国家已经死了。至少现在还不会。\n你体内的力量就是证明，我们能把它重新引导回来。

column5: If the spirits can move power from the land, to an individual?\nWell, there's no reason to believe that the reverse isn't possible.\nThat blade is capable of so much. I think it will be the key to {i}all{/i} of that.
column6: 如果灵能把力量从土地转移到一个人身上？\n那就没有理由认为反过来不可能。\n那把刃能做到的事太多了。我认为它会成为{i}这一切{/i}的关键。

column6: 目前无法访问该内容。\n如果显示叉号，你必须先完成之前的心灵交流。\n如果显示对勾，你必须继续下一个心灵交流。

column5: Hey, this is where I got those apples.\nI still wish they didn't end up scamming me.
column6: 嘿，我就是在这儿买的那些苹果。\n我还是希望他们没骗我。

column5: You can never trust anybody around here.\nEven I get taken advantage of sometimes.
column6: 这地方谁都不能信。\n连我有时候也会被人占便宜。

column5: Really?
column6: 真的？

column5: Yeah. I can let my guard down, too.\nSo don't feel bad about your mistake, Fortaime.
column6: 是啊。我也会有放松警惕的时候。\n所以别为自己的失误难过，福泰姆。

column5: If anything, he learned an important lesson.\nShould we go complain? Maybe he can get his money back.
column6: 往好处想，他学到了重要的一课。\n我们要不要去理论一下？也许能把钱要回来。

column5: There's no point. They'd never give it back.\nWe'd only end up bringing more attention to ourselves.\nI think we'll just have to chalk this one up as a loss.
column6: 没用的。他们绝不会退钱。\n那样只会引来更多注意。\n我看这一笔只能认栽了。

column5: Alright, I'm sorry...
column6: 好吧，对不起……

column5: You didn't do anything wrong. They did.\nI'll buy you more apples when I get a chance.\nThe money I gave you could've easily bought ten.
column6: 你没做错什么。错的是他们。\n有机会我再给你买些苹果。\n我给你那些钱，本来轻轻松松能买十个。

column5: Ten!?
column6: 十个！？

column5: How far back does this Town Square go...?
column6: 这个城广场到底延伸多远……？

column5: To be honest, it almost doesn't stop.\nMazeo is pretty much one huge market.\nThere's a few residential areas, but they're tiny.
column6: 老实说，几乎望不到头。\n马泽奥差不多就是一整个巨型集市。\n有几个住宅区，但都小得很。

column5: That's insane!
column6: 太夸张了！

column5: Yeah, but you get used to it.
column6: 是啊，不过你会习惯的。

column5: Where do the people live then?
column6: 那人们住在哪儿？

column5: Most of them have small beds behind their market stalls.\nThose that are lucky enough to own an actual shop, live inside of it.\nIf you want to live in Mazeo, you need to sell something of value.
column6: 大多数人就在摊位后面搭张小床。\n运气好、能拥有真正店面的人，就住在店里。\n想在马泽奥生活，你就得卖点有价值的东西。

column5: Or offer your services.\nLike me with my sword arm.
column6: 或者靠自己的本事吃饭。\n就像我靠这把剑一样。

column5: Yeah. You need to do {i}something{/i} to make money.\nIf you live in a residential area, that means you're rich.\nIt's a sign of wealth — like you don't need to work anymore.
column6: 是啊。你总得做{i}点什么{/i}来赚钱。\n要是住在住宅区，那就说明你有钱。\n那是财富的象征——好像你再也不用干活了。

column5: I'm guessing not everybody gets that far...
column6: 我猜不是人人都能走到那一步……

column5: No. Most people live on a day-to-day basis.\nIf they don't sell something that day, they don't eat.
column6: 不。大多数人都是过一天算一天。\n那天没卖出东西，就没饭吃。

column5: That's crazy. \nIn Valinorth, we share everything.\nWe'd never stand by while a citizen starves.
column6: 太不可思议了。\n在瓦利诺斯，我们分享一切。\n我们绝不会坐视任何一位同胞挨饿。

column5: Yeah, you have it pretty good in Valinorth.\nBut this is what I like to call the \"real world\", Valessa.\nValinorth was special. The rest of the world is more like {i}this{/i}.
column6: 是啊，你们在瓦利诺斯过得挺不错。\n但这才是我所谓的“现实世界”，瓦莱莎。\n瓦利诺斯是特别的。外面的世界更接近{i}这样{/i}。

column5: Hopefully we can change that...\nWhere do you think we'll be living after the war?
column6: 希望我们能改变这一切……\n你觉得战后我们会住在哪儿？

column5: If we survive? \nWherever we want.
column6: 如果我们能活下来？\n想住哪儿住哪儿。

column5: Wow, you can buy weapons here?\nI mean, they're just laying out in the open.
column6: 哇，这里能买到武器？\n我是说，它们就那么露天摆着。

column5: Yeah. You can buy anything in Mazeo.\nIf it's not legal, then the pirates can get it for you. \nThey call this place the town of \"Infinite Connections\".
column6: 是啊。在马泽奥什么都能买到。\n要是合法的买不到，海盗能帮你弄来。\n他们管这里叫“无穷人脉”之城。

column5: Wow...
Hey, that one looks like your sword, Ulric.\nDid you buy your sword from one of these places?
column6: 嘿，那把看起来像你的剑，乌尔里克。\n你的剑是从这种地方买的吗？

column5: No. My sword is ancient.\nRumor says it belonged to an Alarinthian legend.\nWith just how well it's made — I think that's actually true.
column6: 不是。我的剑年代久远。\n据说它曾属于一位阿拉林西亚的传奇人物。\n光看它做工之精——我觉得那传言是真的。

column5: Wow, a legend?\nExplains why you carry it around all the time.
column6: 哇，传奇人物？\n难怪你总是随身带着它。

column5: Yeah, I'd hate to leave it unattended.\nEven when I carry it, people beg me to sell it.\nBut it beats leaving it alone, and risking theft.
column6: 是啊，我可不想让它无人看管。\n就算我随身带着，也有人求我卖给他。\n但总好过放着被人偷走。

column5: So you've used that sword for your entire life?
column6: 那你一辈子都在用那把剑？

column5: I have; and I'll use it for the rest of my life, too.\nIt shows no signs of wearing down. It's perfect.\nI can't say the same about the ones {i}they{/i} have for sale.
column6: 是的；我余生也会一直用它。\n它没有任何磨损的迹象。完美无缺。\n{i}他们{/i}卖的那些我可不敢这么说。

column5: Ulric motions at the market stall that initially got Valessa's attention.{w}\nThe merchant glances over at us, understanding Ulric's accusatory gesture.{w}\nWe quickly run away from the stall before they can speak or chase after us.
column6: 乌尔里克朝最初引得瓦莱莎注意的那个摊位示意。{w}\n那商人瞥了我们一眼，明白了乌尔里克那透着指责的手势。{w}\n还没等对方开口或追来，我们就赶紧从摊位前溜走了。
